The api died at 03:14:06 because the `report-export` job filled the `/var/lib/stockroom` disk, and it never came back for the rest of the log.

One thing to check first: the log's timestamps are all 2026-03-09 (02:00–05:29), not last night, so this may be a sample or stale file rather than the outage you mean.

What the log shows:

- **03:05:00** – `report-export` starts writing 512 MB CSV parts to `/var/lib/stockroom/exports/`, one every 12 seconds.
- **03:09:03** – first warning: `disk /var/lib/stockroom at 91%`. The export keeps going.
- **03:12:48** – last export part written, 40 parts in all (about 20 GB in under 8 minutes).
- **03:13:30** – `disk /var/lib/stockroom at 99%`.
- **03:14:00** – `db: could not extend file "base/16384/2619": No space left on device`.
- **03:14:03** – `api: transaction aborted, shutting down worker pool`.
- **03:14:06** – `FATAL api: exiting (status 1)`.
- **03:16:00 onward** – `proxy: upstream api refused connection` every 2 minutes, 66 times, through 05:28:00.

After the fatal line there is not a single api request in the log, so the api was still down when the log ends at 05:29:57, at least 2h15m of outage. `web` and `proxy` kept serving 200s throughout.

The log has no api restart or startup line, even though compose sets `restart: unless-stopped` on it. The log doesn't say why. It also doesn't show whether the disk was ever freed.

The `cache: slow command` warnings (43 of them, 100–150 ms) run at a steady rate from 02:00 to the end of the log, before and after the crash, so they look unrelated.
